title: Fidelity Charitable Program Guidelines (Terms and Conditions)
pinpoint: 'Donors, Account Holders, and Authorized Persons' (Fidelity Charitable approval; General - no testamentary instructions); Authorized Person 'Termination of privileges'; 'Termination of Giving Account privileges'; Grants: 'Remedial actions', 'Minimum grant requirements - Each Giving Account'; Legacy (pp.13-14): Successor Account Holder, 90-day response, unrestricted funds default; Miscellaneous: 'Confidentiality'
summary: Only Account Holders/Authorized Persons designated by an Account Holder exercise privileges; no testamentary or posthumous instructions; Fidelity may revoke privileges in sole discretion. Inactivity: contact after 1 year, Trustee grants after 2 years; grants to other DAF sponsors do not count as activity. Successor accounts created per successor percentage; 90-day nonresponse sends balance to unrestricted funds.

title: Vanguard Charitable Policies and Guidelines (January 2026)
pinpoint: p.3-4 'Account structure' (death/incapacity of an advisor; successor advisor; 'Termination of account privileges' incl. freeze while under investigation); 'Account granting activity - Minimum Account Activity' (30 months inactive; one $500 grant every three years); Legacy options p.19-20 'Enacting a succession plan' (abandoned account; death certificate; durable POA accepted as proof of incapacity)
summary: On death/incapacity of one advisor the remaining advisor keeps privileges; succession enacted on abandonment, proof of last advisor's death, or written proof of incapacity (a durable POA is accepted as proof). Privileges may be limited, suspended or revoked; account may be frozen while an advisor is under investigation. Inactive after 30 months; Vanguard may grant per succession plan, history or its own funds.

title: DAFgiving360 Program Policies (Updated December 2024)
effective_date: 2024-12 (a 2026 revision is indexed but dafgiving360.org returned 403 to prior research; not read)
pinpoint: 'Account privilege limitations' (limit/suspend/terminate; freeze until resolution of investigation; court orders); 'Recommending grants' inactivity (30 months inactive; further 2 years dormant; closure to granting history or Philanthropy Fund); Section 7 Succession planning p.31 incl. footnote 14 (executor/trustee cannot exercise privileges unless also a successor)
summary: Privileges may be limited, suspended or terminated and assets granted out; account may be frozen pending investigation by authorities or acted on under court orders. Inactive after 30 months; dormant after a further two years; succession plan enacted or account closed to granting history/Philanthropy Fund. Executors/trustees cannot exercise privileges unless named successors; one new account per successor.

title: A Guide to your Donor-Advised Fund (NPT)
effective_date: uploaded 2024-09 (prior research recorded a 2026-10 revision at same URL)
pinpoint: 'Legacy Plan' (activated on notification of death of last primary/joint advisor; written evidence of death; perpetual succession; separate accounts per successor); 'Inactive Donor-Advised Funds' (six consecutive years without grant recommendations = abandoned, Legacy Plan); 'Account Balance Minimum Policy' (90-day outreach then NPT Giving Fund)
summary: NPT owns all DAF assets; Legacy Plan activates on written evidence of the last advisor's death; successors get separate accounts and may name further successors. A DAF with no grant recommendations for six consecutive years is deemed abandoned and the Legacy Plan applies; low-balance accounts get 90-day notices before transfer to the NPT Giving Fund.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4966 Taxes on taxable distributions
issuer: U.S. Congress (LII mirror of U.S. Code)
pinpoint: §4966(c)(1) taxable distribution; §4966(c)(2)(A)-(C) exceptions (170(b)(1)(A) org other than disqualified supporting org; the sponsoring organization; any other donor advised fund); §4966(d)(2)(A)(i)-(iii) DAF definition ('owned and controlled by a sponsoring organization'; donor 'or any person appointed or designated by such donor')
summary: Distributions from a DAF to a 170(b)(1)(A) organization (not a disqualified supporting org), to its own sponsoring organization, or to any other DAF are not taxable distributions. A DAF is owned and controlled by the sponsor; advisory privileges belong to the donor or persons the donor appoints or designates.

title: Rev. Proc. 2018-32, 2018-23 I.R.B.
pinpoint: §3.02 (TEOS/Pub.78 data generally updated monthly), §3.05 (EO BMF extract monthly), §3.06 (Auto-Revocation List monthly); §4.01, §4.02, §4.04; §5.01 (sponsoring organizations of DAFs may rely on public charity status for §4966 grantmaking), §5.02; §6.01-6.03; §11 (supersedes Rev. Procs. 81-6, 81-7, 89-23, 2011-33); §12 effective 2018-05-16
summary: Grantors may rely on TEOS/BMF listings until a public announcement of loss of status (or, for auto-revocation, posting on the list), unless they knew of, were aware of imminent, or were partly responsible for the revocation. Sponsoring organizations may rely on listed public charity status for §4966 purposes. Databases are generally updated monthly.

title: Taxes on Taxable Distributions From Donor Advised Funds Under Section 4966 (proposed rule) 88 FR 77922
pinpoint: Prop. Treas. Reg. §53.4966-1(h)(1) donor-advisor ('No particular form of appointment or designation is necessary'; delegatees are donor-advisors); Prop. §53.4966-5 non-taxable distributions incl. '(iii) Any other donor advised fund' and '(3) Special rule' (series of distributions under a plan treated as single distribution); preamble 'distribution' includes any transfer in cash or in kind
summary: Proposed rules would treat anyone appointed or designated by a donor (no particular form) and their delegatees as donor-advisors, keep DAF-to-DAF distributions non-taxable, and collapse a series of distributions made under a plan inconsistent with §4966. Not effective law.

title: Federal Register API search: documents matching '4966 donor advised' since 2024-01-01; IRS Rules matching 'donor advised fund'
pinpoint: Results list: 2024-00260 (proposed rule, 2024-01-09), 2024-04262 and 2024-08419 (hearing notices); no final rule. IRS Rule-type search for 'donor advised fund' since 2024 returns only 'Trump Accounts' (2026-09-30).
summary: As of 2026-11-24 the Federal Register contains no final rule under §4966; the 2023 proposed regulations remain proposed (secondary reporting says the Spring 2026 regulatory agenda targeted July 2026 for finalization, which did not occur in the Register).

title: Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006, as amended 2008/2011) with comments
issuer: Uniform Law Commission (NCCUSL) - copy hosted by Alaska Bar
source_type: uniform act (model; law only where enacted)
pinpoint: §119 (good-faith reliance; certification/opinion requests); §120 (accept or request certification within 7 business days; refusal grounds (b)(1)-(6) incl. not otherwise required to transact, good-faith belief agent lacks authority, APS report); §201(a) (express grant required to make a gift etc., and only if 'not otherwise prohibited by another agreement or instrument to which the authority or property is subject'); §217 gifts default limits
summary: Agents need express authority to make gifts of the principal's property; another agreement governing the authority can prohibit exercise. Third parties must accept an acknowledged POA or request certification within seven business days unless a statutory refusal ground applies, with fee-shifting for wrongful refusal; good-faith acceptors are protected.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. §32C-2-201 and §32C-2-217 (NC Uniform Power of Attorney Act)
pinpoint: §32C-2-201(a)(1)a (make a gift only if expressly granted), (b) consistency with principal's objectives incl. 'personal history of making or joining in making gifts', (c) no self-benefit; §32C-2-217(b)(1)b (general gift authority covers gifts to §170(c)/2522(a) organizations 'in accordance with the principal's history')
summary: Enacted UPOAA variant: gift authority must be express; general gift authority reaches charitable gifts only in line with the principal's giving history; agent may not create interests in itself. Illustrates state divergence from uniform text (NC adds charitable-history clause, opinion-of-counsel and APS refusal grounds).

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. §32C-1-119 and §32C-1-120 (acceptance of and refusal to accept POA)
pinpoint: §32C-1-120(b)(1) seven business days; (c)(1) 'not otherwise required to engage in a transaction with the principal in the same circumstances'; (c)(6)-(7) good-faith doubt; (c)(9) APS/law-enforcement report; (d)(3) no duty to permit unauthorized business; (e) court order and fees
summary: A person presented with an acknowledged POA must accept, refuse on a listed ground, or request certification within seven business days; listed grounds include no independent duty to transact, good-faith doubt about authority or appropriateness, and a report of suspected exploitation to APS or law enforcement.

title: Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 18-C §5-414 (UGCOPAA enactment): conservator powers requiring court approval
pinpoint: §5-414(1) lead-in (notice and specific court authorization); (1)(A) make gifts except de minimis; (1)(D) exercise or release a power of appointment
summary: Under this Uniform Guardianship, Conservatorship and Other Protective Arrangements Act enactment, a conservator needs specific court authorization, after notice, to make non-de-minimis gifts or exercise powers of appointment.

title: FINRA Rule 2165 (Financial Exploitation of Specified Adults)
source_type: SRO rule (binds FINRA members only; analogy)
pinpoint: (a)(1) Specified Adult; (b)(1) hold on disbursement or securities transaction on reasonable belief of exploitation; (b)(1)(B) notice within 2 business days with exception where party believed involved; (b)(2) 15 business days; (b)(3) +10 business days; (b)(4) +30 business days if reported to state regulator/agency or court; termination/extension by regulator or court
summary: Permits, but does not require, member firms to place temporary holds where exploitation is reasonably believed; notice within two business days except to suspected parties; maximum 15+10+30 business days with internal review and regulator/court reporting. Applies only to FINRA members; a DAF sponsor may borrow the design.

title: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-05; SR-FINRA-2026-018 (proposed further amendments to Rules 2165, 4512 and new Rule 2166)
pinpoint: Search-result summaries only (not fetched): Notice 22-05 announces effective date 2022-03-17 for 30-business-day extension and securities-transaction holds; SR-FINRA-2026-018 filed 2026 with SIFMA comment dated 2026-09-30.
summary: Confirms the 2022 amendment date; a further 2026 FINRA filing on Rule 2165 is pending at the SEC and could change durations. Not fetched; reconsideration trigger only.

title: 12 U.S.C. §3423 (Senior Safe Act, Pub. L. 115-174 §303)
pinpoint: §3423(a)(1)(D) covered financial institution (credit unions, depository institutions, investment advisers, broker-dealers, insurers, insurance agencies, transfer agents); (a)(2) immunity for good-faith, reasonable-care disclosures to covered agencies incl. APS; (b) training
summary: Grants immunity for good-faith reports of suspected senior exploitation by trained employees of listed financial institutions to regulators, law enforcement or APS. It does not authorize holds, and a 501(c)(3) DAF sponsor is not a listed covered institution.

title: Tax Exempt Organization Search bulk data downloads
pinpoint: 'The data set files are updated monthly'; Publication 78 data last updated Nov. 11, 2026; Automatic revocation list last updated Nov. 11, 2026
summary: IRS states TEOS bulk files are updated monthly; on 2026-11-24 Pub. 78 and auto-revocation files showed 2026-11-11 as last update.

title: Exempt Organizations Business Master File Extract (EO BMF)
pinpoint: 'Updated data posting date: 11/10/2026'; 'This is a cumulative file, and the data are the most recent information the IRS has'
summary: EO BMF extract last posted 2026-11-10; page gives no cadence (Rev. Proc. 2018-32 §3.05 says generally monthly).

title: 26 C.F.R. §1.6001-1 Records
pinpoint: §1.6001-1(c) exempt organizations keep permanent books sufficient to show gross income, receipts and disbursements and to substantiate §6033 information; §1.6001-1(e) retain 'so long as the contents thereof may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law'
summary: Exempt organizations must keep books showing receipts and disbursements and substantiating Form 990 information, retained as long as material to tax administration. The duty is the organization's (the sponsor's), not its software vendor's.

title: Publication 4221-PC, Compliance Guide for 501(c)(3) Public Charities (Rev. 3-2018)
pinpoint: p.14 'How Long Should Records be Kept?' (generally until statute of limitations runs, generally 3 years after return due/filed, later of; longer for other legal purposes) and 'Record Retention Periods' (permanent: exemption application, determination letter, organizing documents, board minutes; employment tax records 4 years)
summary: Public charities keep records supporting return items until the limitation period runs (generally three years after the later of due or filing date), longer where other laws require; certain governance records permanently.

title: Instructions for Schedule N (Form 990) - IRS annotated 2024 form and instructions
pinpoint: Part II instructions: significant disposition = >25% of FMV of net assets incl. series of related dispositions; excluded: 'Grants or other assistance made in the ordinary course of the organization's exempt activities to accomplish the organization's exempt purposes'
summary: Organizations disposing of more than 25% of net assets (alone or via related series) report on Schedule N Part II; grants in the ordinary course of exempt activities are excluded. A one-time program transfer may fall outside 'ordinary course'.

title: California Corporations Code §5913 (notice to Attorney General of disposition of all or substantially all assets)
pinpoint: §5913: written notice to the Attorney General 20 days before sale/transfer of all or substantially all assets, except in the usual and regular course of activities or with AG waiver
summary: A California public benefit corporation must give the Attorney General 20 days' written notice before transferring all or substantially all assets outside the usual course. Illustrates state charity-regulator gates on sponsor-initiated program transfers.

title: California Civil Code §47(c) (common-interest privileged publication)
pinpoint: §47(c) communications 'without malice, to a person interested therein' by (1) one also interested, (2) one with relationship giving reasonable grounds for innocent motive, or (3) one requested by the interested person
summary: California codifies the common-interest qualified privilege: non-malicious communications between interested persons are privileged. The privilege is qualified (lost on malice) and state-specific.

title: Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 13 §5103 (UPMIFA standard of conduct in managing and investing institutional funds)
pinpoint: §5103(2) good faith and care of an ordinarily prudent person; §5103(5)(D) duty to diversify unless special circumstances
summary: Charities managing institutional funds must act in good faith with ordinary prudence and diversify. Supports continuing the sponsor's standing investment policy during an advisory dispute rather than freezing investments.

title: daf-landscape research: Bequests, legacy DAFs and succession terms (b49-03)
issuer: Unbound research repository (internal; secondary compilation of sponsor documents)
pinpoint: §2 findings 2-3; table rows 1-15 (default with no successor; successor caps SVCF 3, CCT 2 generations, FFTC 1; MS GIFT pays named charities after 5 years with no successor grant; JCF bypasses successors after 1 year nonresponse)
summary: Compiles 15 sponsors' succession terms: 11 default un-planned balances to the sponsor's own pool; four cap successor generations; nonresponse windows vary (Fidelity 90 days, JCF 1 year). Read locally, not re-fetched; Fidelity/Vanguard/NPT/DAFgiving360 rows re-verified here.

title: daf-landscape research: State charity filings, outbound transfer terms and DAF-to-DAF flows
pinpoint: P-QA3-02 row; sponsor table rows (Fidelity, DAFgiving360, NPT, NCF, AEF); BNY Mellon fund collapsed into RCF (sponsor-initiated bulk transfer)
summary: No sponsor publishes an outbound-transfer procedure; NCF bars succession funds from granting to other DAF sponsors; AEF reviews dormant funds after 36 months; BNY Mellon's DAF program moved to RCF as a sponsor-initiated bulk transfer; Form 990 Schedule I shows nine-figure DAF-to-DAF flows. Not re-fetched.

title: daf-landscape research: escheat of voided DAF grant checks (batch 34C)
summary: Unclaimed-property statutes cover nonprofit holders and checks; voided gift checks have 'without consideration' and void defences; no enforcement history found. Relevant to residual balances at closure only by analogy; DAF balances themselves are sponsor-owned. Not re-fetched.
